claims.text: The target material is a multiphase AlxCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with x approximately 1.3.
As-cast Al1.3CoCrFeNi contains disordered FCC, disordered BCC, and incipient B2-ordered phases.
The initial microstructure has nanoscale chemical heterogeneity.
Aging between 400°C and 800°C for 100 to 10,000 hours promotes chemical ordering and phase evolution in Al1.3CoCrFeNi.
Thermal aging produces a ductile-brittle-ductile transition in Al1.3CoCrFeNi.
The transition is driven by sequential evolution from short-range order to B2 long-range order and then to phase separation.
The intermediate brittle state coincides with the peak stability or maximum amount of B2 long-range order.
The ordering-onset temperature in AlxCoCrFeNi depends strongly on Al content.
The ordering-onset temperature is approximately 600°C to 1200°C for compositions between x=1 and x=2.
Phase separation produces Ni/Co/Al-rich B2 regions and Fe/Cr-rich disordered regions.
B2 ordering is driven by Al-Ni and Al-Co interactions.
Chemical ordering can change mechanical behavior through interactions with dislocations and altered cross-slip.
Strong B2 long-range order increases lattice friction and restricts cross-slip.
B2 decomposes or loses long-range order through phase separation near 600°C in AlxCoCrFeNi.
The decomposition or weakening of B2 order relieves lattice constraints and restores ductility.
Elongation to failure has a distinct intermediate-time minimum that coincides with peak B2 order and precedes significant phase separation.
For x=1, B2 order is lost near 1400°C.
For x=2, B2 remains ordered up to melting.
The x=1 and x=2 baseline alloys do not exhibit the proposed intermediate brittle window.
Al-rich compositions with x greater than 1 thermodynamically favor B2 ordering.

contradictions.description: The conditions and boundary place the ordering-onset range at approximately 600–1200°C for x=1 to 2, whereas the baseline states that x=1 loses B2 order near 1400°C. These temperature assertions are internally inconsistent.
